name: Wes Streeting
role: UK Secretary of State for Defence (since July 2026); Labour MP for Ilford North (since 2015); Health and Social Care Secretary 2024-2026
summary: Labour MP and former NUS president who identifies with the revisionist, social-democratic wing of the party, combining support for a publicly funded NHS open to independent-sector capacity, tax reform on wealth, trade unions and an active state with pro-growth, pro-business, pro-NATO and pro-nuclear-deterrent positions. A former Remain campaigner, he now says Britain should rejoin the EU one day, and he backs Israel's right to exist alongside Palestinian statehood and criticism of its conduct in Gaza. He opposes assisted dying and is a supporter of LGBT rights who has taken a cautious, sex-based line on trans issues and puberty blockers.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Told the Commons on 2 December 2025 the government was 'restating the case for universal healthcare that is publicly owned, publicly funded and free at the point of use', and repeatedly vowed to defend the NHS free at the point of use.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Wrote that 'the liberal market settlement born of Thatcherism is not up to the job' and that the market alone will not deliver green industry, and in 2026 said growth needs 'an active state'; but he also calls himself pro-enterprise and says capitalism is the worst system 'except for all the others'. Mixed, so low.

public-ownership.rationale: In 2020 he criticised Labour's 2019 nationalisation plans as ideological and unpriced, yet cited the East Coast mainline as a viable model of 'autonomous state-sponsored companies' and wanted each proposal judged case by case. Points both ways.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Campaigned in 2026 on 'a wealth tax that works': equalising capital gains tax with income tax to raise up to £12bn; in 2020 argued for 'a greater focus on wealth taxation'; as Health Secretary defended ending non-dom status and VAT on private school fees.

unions-good.rationale: Contested: in 2015 he told the Commons the Trade Union Bill went against the best British traditions, but as Health Secretary he called the resident doctors' strikes morally reprehensible and attacked the BMA.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that the state 'needs to regulate effectively to ensure fairness and competition', that monopolies and oligopolies should be broken up and gig-economy firms face tougher enforcement; in 2026 called for strengthening laws against platforms like X.

cut-welfare.rationale: Told the Commons in December 2025 that the Tory 'myth and lie' was that welfare recipients 'are on the take' and said he would not set arbitrary targets to cut the welfare bill, but also said people 'trapped in the benefits system want to escape' and backed reform to reduce the bill via work. Mixed, so low.

worker-ownership.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that the country 'would benefit if more businesses were to become cooperatives or employee-owned like John Lewis' and proposed tax incentives for owners who hand firms to employees, while rejecting compulsory share transfers.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Argued in the Commons in November 2024 that the libertarian case against the smoking ban would lead to asking 'why not legalise cannabis? Why not legalise cocaine?' and treated tobacco as uniquely harmful, using the point as a reductio.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: In 2026 called a misleading political advert 'incitement to hatred' and said that if the law against platforms inciting mob rule is not enforced it should be, and if too weak it should be strengthened.

strong-leader.rationale: Praised Trump as 'a winner and a bulldozer' who gets things done and says Britain's system is too slow ('where there are barriers, we bulldoze them'), but added 'I don't think you come in and tear everything up' and defends Parliament's role.

state-harmful.rationale: Told RCOG in 2025 that those of the left 'fundamentally believe in an active state', and in 2026 that 'we can't create a healthier society without the state'; wants a smarter, more effective state, not a smaller one.

empower-police-military.rationale: Told the Commons in 2019 that police cuts meant 'there has never been a better time to be a criminal' and argued for restoring police funding; as Defence Secretary says Britain must 'invest more heavily in our defence, and more rapidly'.

decide-locally.rationale: Calls himself 'a big fan of devolution' and as Health Secretary pushed power to the frontline and metro mayors, but in 2026 said he would take planning decisions from councils that miss housing targets. Mixed, so low.

rehabilitation.rationale: No recorded position. His remarks on why offender rehabilitation matters do not weigh rehabilitation against punishment as the aim of prisons.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Told the Commons in 2016 that the legalisation of equal marriage made 'our country a better place', and in 2023 said he would vote for permissive legislation letting churches marry same-sex couples; he is himself gay.

abortion-legal.rationale: Told the Commons in October 2018 that it was an anomaly that in Northern Ireland women could not 'seek access to safe and legal abortion' and that it was 'time to end that anomaly'.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that the UK 'will need to recruit people from overseas' and wanted a points-based system; in 2026 said 'yes we need to control our borders, yes we need to deal with the boats' while backing a global talent drive and the Home Secretary's earned settlement plans. Points both ways.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that Britain should 'seek to strengthen key institutions like the UN, NATO and the Bretton Woods Institutions' and rebuild global institutions because 'global problems require global solutions'.

free-trade.rationale: Argued the single market and customs union helped UK trade, but wrote that globalisation was 'a construct of political decisions' to be managed and that its benefits were unevenly shared.

nation-first.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that 'global problems require global solutions' and said in 2026 that nationalism says 'look inward' while patriotism is 'outward looking, generous' and internationalist.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that a Labour government should uphold the responsibility to protect, citing Bosnia, Kosovo and Sierra Leone as British action that 'saved countless lives' and Rwanda and Syria as failures to act.

open-borders.rationale: Said in May 2026 that the case for Europe was about sovereignty 'and the need to control our borders', and repeated 'yes, we need to control our borders' in a 2026 interview.

limit-growth.rationale: In 2026 said growth should be 'the number one priority', that the Greens 'don't really believe in growth' and that is 'the road to nowhere', and proposed loosening environmental assessment thresholds for housing.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that there is a climate emergency requiring a UK Green New Deal as a national mission, and in 2026 backed going 'big on renewables'.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that 'nuclear energy will continue to be a key source of our energy supply if we want to decarbonise with the urgency required'.

experts-over-public.rationale: Said expert leaders are among the most effective public service reforms, but also that politicians exist 'to put the patient first' and that 'public services exist to serve the public, not their producers'.

central-planning.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that 'the Labour party is not an anti-capitalist party' and, paraphrasing Churchill, that capitalism is 'the worst economic system except for all those other systems which have been tried'.

tax-inheritance.rationale: In 2020 called inheritance tax 'indefensible' because the rich avoid it and proposed capping or scrapping reliefs or a lifetime gifts tax, but also wrote that we should 'care less about how we tax the dead'; in 2026 called it the 'third rail' needing careful reform. Mixed, so low.

basic-income.rationale: In 2020 said Labour's idea of universal basic income trials 'raised more questions than answers' and left the party exposed, treating UBI only as a possible long-term necessity if mass unemployment came.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Backed a mission-led industrial strategy, a green investment bank and state-led R&D in 2020 ('the market alone will not provide'), and as Defence Secretary describes defence spending as investment for reindustrialisation and growth.

democracy-best.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that democracy, freedom and human rights must be defended against populists and that Labour's defining mission includes extending them; also told the Commons the result of the Brexit referendum must be abided by even though he opposed it.

right-to-secede.rationale: Told the Commons in June 2020 'we are stronger together' on the Union, and in May 2026 called Scottish and Welsh nationalism 'an existential threat to the future integrity of the United Kingdom'.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Told the Commons on 20 May 2026 that his patriotism is 'built not on blood and soil but on shared values, shared institutions and shared responsibilities' and cited the son of Indian pharmacists becoming Prime Minister.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Told IPPR in 2024 he would take on 'the ideologues who do not believe the NHS should have any relationship with the private sector', and said in 2026 there is a difference 'between being an ideologue and ideologically informed'.

harm-principle.rationale: Backed the generational smoking ban, telling the Commons in November 2024 'there is no liberty in addiction' and rejecting the live-and-let-live libertarian case; as minister defended 'nanny state' public health reforms.

positive-liberty.rationale: In his January 2026 Progress speech endorsed the New Liberal view that 'liberty is not merely freedom from interference but freedom to act' and said 'freedom is hollow if it is hoarded'.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Told the Commons in July 2017 'I have never supported those who wish to delegitimise the state of Israel' and in 2026 repeated 'Israel's right to exist and to defend itself', describing a democratic and Jewish state.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Proposed in 2020 that every public and private organisation with more than 250 employees have elected employee representation on boards and remuneration committees.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: In May 2026 said he would stick to Rachel Reeves's fiscal rules because with debt over 100% of GDP 'playing fast and loose' pushes up borrowing costs and crowds out public services.

national-self-determination.rationale: Supports 'the right of Palestinians to a state of their own' but opposes Scottish and Welsh independence and secession. Points both ways.

reason-over-faith.rationale: In 2026 said R.H. Tawney's ethical Christian socialism 'speaks to my values and my faith', and in 2019 described himself as a Christian whose views are informed by theology.

class-collaboration.rationale: Said in 2026 that 'government and business are not in competition. Employer and workers do not need to be in competition', and that growth and fairness go together.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Said in May 2026 that patriotism is 'united, but not always the same' and rooted in welcoming difference, and told the Commons in 2019 schools should celebrate 'diversity and difference'.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that 'outright gender discrimination exists and is entrenched by this economic structure' and in 2026 described 'everyday sexism and a boys' club right at the heart of government'.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: As Defence Secretary said in October 2026 that veterans who served in Northern Ireland should not face an 'endless cycle of reinvestigation', while the Troubles Bill he backs scrapped the Legacy Act immunity scheme and aims at 'truth, integrity and accountability for all communities'. Points both ways.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that 'all human beings are born equal', and said in 2026 that 'the lives of Israelis and Palestinians are of equal worth and value'.

separated-powers.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that the Conservative government 'persistently threatens judicial independence', needed to be taken to court over an illegal prorogation and resisted media scrutiny, defending checks on executive power.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Told the Commons in 2015 the Trade Union Bill's higher ballot thresholds were 'sinister, shabby and shameful' and wanted electronic balloting; in 2020 listed repeal of the 2016 Trade Union Act as 'practical common sense'.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Wrote in 2020 of 'our belief that diversity is a strength' as the Labour value that populists and nativists reject, and in 2026 described Britain's strength as people of different backgrounds standing beside one another.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Said in 2026 that Labour needs a culture that does not shut down debate, that amending legislation should not be treated as disloyalty, and that unity should not be 'the unity of the graveyard where everyone has to be robots'.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Told the Commons in 2016 that 'if we pool our sovereignty and work together with our partners ... we have greater weight', and said in May 2026 that Brexit was a 'catastrophic mistake' and that he would like to see Britain back in the EU one day.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: As Defence Secretary says defence runs 'primarily through NATO first and foremost' and is deepening alliance integration; wrote in 2020 that NATO is the cornerstone of British defence.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Told the Commons in March 2019 he 'warmly' supported the relationships and sex education regulations as 'a modest measure' that 'does not go far enough' and criticised parents' right to withdraw children from sex education.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that the 0.7% aid commitment should be maintained and 'resolutely defended', with every penny spent on genuine aid and development; no later stated change.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that any prime minister must have 'both the means and the will' to respond to a nuclear strike and said in September 2026 that supporting the nuclear deterrent is something he believes 'very strongly'; voted to replace the Vanguard-class submarines.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Has long backed a two-state solution with 'a secure and viable Palestinian state alongside a secure state of Israel', called the West Bank occupation and settlement expansion illegal and called for sanctions on settlements.

collective-defense.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that Labour should be 'unequivocal about our support for NATO and our commitment to Article 5', and as Defence Secretary calls NATO 'absolutely critical'.

ban-cartels.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that Labour is 'determined to break up monopolies and oligopolies' and opposes excessive concentrations of corporate power.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: As Health Secretary launched a men's health strategy, saying he is 'just as enraged about the inequalities in men's health' and that men and boys face injustices (shorter lives, suicide, falling behind at school) that need action alongside women's health.

paid-care-work.rationale: No recorded position. His remarks on unpaid care's value and Carer's Allowance are a related point; he did not address paying for domestic work generally.

non-intervention.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that 'the international community has a clear obligation to intervene' where a government fails to protect its citizens, including sanctions and military action.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that Labour's antisemitism stemmed from a worldview 'that puts Jews or Zionists at the centre of a global capitalist conspiracy' that voters found repulsive and that must be abandoned, and condemned classic tropes about Jewish money and power.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Said in 2026 that Britain wrote the UN Charter and international law that 'stands against tyranny' and must keep doing so, and in September 2026 welcomed the ECHR being invoked in a positive context.

religious-nation.rationale: Described the nation in May 2026 as people 'from different backgrounds, different faiths, and different nations and regions' who see themselves in one another, explicitly not defined by blood and soil.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: As Health Secretary vowed to 'rid my department and the NHS of any cultural sniffiness about dealing with the private sector' and attacked 'ideologues' opposed to it; in January 2025 announced an agreement for NHS patients to be treated in private hospitals at state expense.

religion-illusion.rationale: In 2024 described himself as an Anglican who believes in the Virgin birth and the resurrection, and in 2019 told the Commons 'as a Christian' that all are created in God's image.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Told the Commons on Holocaust Memorial Day in 2016 and 2021 that the Nazis 'perpetrated appalling acts of genocide' and that the Holocaust must be taught and remembered.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: As an openly gay MP told the Commons in 2016 that the abolition of discriminatory laws had made the country 'a better place', backed pardons for convictions of gay men, and in 2026 celebrated gay people serving openly.

participatory-democracy.rationale: In 2026 said services should put 'power, agency, choice and control into the hands of service users' and trust people 'as experts in their own lives', and in 2020 proposed elected employee representatives on company boards.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Told the Commons in June 2020 that discrimination 'is often intersectional' and that people face it 'twofold, threefold or fourfold' across gender, race, disability and poverty, though protected characteristics are listed one by one.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Says trans people deserve 'dignity and freedom' and backed trans-specific wards or 'third spaces' alongside sex-based spaces, banned puberty blockers for under-18s, and said in 2024 he no longer stood by 'trans women are women'; no stance on legal gender recognition itself. Points both ways.

assisted-dying.rationale: Voted against the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill at second reading in November 2024 and against it again in later divisions; warned on Facebook that assisted dying in the NHS would take 'time and money' and 'there isn't a budget for this', and echoed Gordon Brown's concern that patients may feel pressure to relieve relatives of their care.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Talks of unifying progressives and combining wealth creation with fairness, but also says there are 'big dividing lines' between 'our left and right' and calls himself from the revisionist wing of Labour. Points both ways.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Opened the 2019 Commons debate defending the APPG definition of Islamophobia, said in 2019 he would defend Muslim constituents' 'religious freedom and place in the community', and in 2026 described anti-Muslim abuse as racism to be confronted.

social-market-economy.rationale: Describes himself as a mainstream social democrat who is both 'pro wealth creation and pro wealth distribution', backs Danish-style flexicurity with social protection, and says growth and fairness 'go hand in hand'; rejects both Green anti-growth and Tory no-active-state approaches.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: As Defence Secretary says Britain must be able to 'deter and, if necessary, defeat' adversaries and be war-fighting ready by 2030, and is expanding defence investment.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Calls himself 'an Atlanticist as well as a very strong pro-European' and puts NATO first in defence policy.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that citizens' assemblies like those used in Ireland on same-sex marriage and abortion 'might help create the conditions' for lasting social care reform and that their findings on climate should inform policy.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Told the Commons in 2017 that vast untaxed wealth gained by luck has 'a corrosive impact on politics itself' because people feel the system serves a privileged few; in January 2026 said freedom is 'hollow if it is hoarded'.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: As Defence Secretary said in October 2026 that the dismissal of gay personnel was a failure of the country, welcomed more than 2,500 openly LGBTQ+ personnel and pledged support for LGBT and trans service members.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Argued in 2019 for restoring police numbers and funding ('never been a better time to be a criminal') and wrote in 2020 that Labour should return to being 'tough on crime and tough on the causes of crime' with criminal activity 'met with justice'.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that 'it is unacceptable that those who have worked hard end up paying more in tax than those who have gained from investments or dividends' and backed taxing capital gains like earnings.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Told the Commons in December 2025 the NHS must remain 'publicly owned, publicly funded and free at the point of use'; he said nothing on water or local transport ownership.

family-wage.rationale: Told the Commons in 2020 'it should never be the case that where people are going out to work ... earning money for themselves and their families, they should still find themselves living in conditions of poverty', and in 2025 spoke of restoring the link between a hard day's work and a fair day's pay.

person-over-state.rationale: Said in January 2026 that 'public services exist to serve the public, not their producers' and that they should be designed around the citizen and trust people 'as experts in their own lives'.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Backed the responsibility to protect and military intervention to save lives (Kosovo, Sierra Leone), while opposing the Iraq war; he does not limit force to self-defence.

free-public-college.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that tuition fees should be abolished and replaced by a graduate tax, but also that free undergraduate tuition was 'the wrong priority' compared with early years and adult education. Points both ways.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that the tax system should 'create and enforce incentives and disincentives to tackle polluting behaviour' and reward long-term green investment.

future-generations.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that 'we are temporary custodians of the world that we share together and each of us has a responsibility to care for our environment'.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that collective bargaining rights had been eroded, that it should be easier to gain union recognition, and that employment rights should be 'negotiated between employers and trades unions', pointing to Australian and New Zealand sector bargaining models.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Told the Commons in October 2015 that tax credits are 'a well-targeted tax rebate' for low-paid people who work hard and that cutting them was 'a shameful measure'.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: No recorded position. Support for keeping the government's fiscal rules is a related point; he did not say they should be legally binding.

public-service-media.rationale: Said in 2026 the creation of the BBC as a public service broadcaster, rather than leaving it to the market, was a great British institution; in 2020 wrote that the BBC should be invested in and defended against attacks.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Wrote in 2020 'we do not believe the world would be safer if our enemies had a monopoly on nuclear weapons' while committing to multilateral disarmament, and as Defence Secretary backs the deterrent.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Asked the Government in 2017 to press Sri Lanka to ratify the Rome Statute with international judges and prosecutors involved, and in 2026 said international courts should determine through evidence whether Israel's actions amount to war crimes or genocide.

close-ties-china.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that Britain's relationship with the US and China 'cannot be equidistant', that the US is 'our natural ally', while seeking cooperation and trade with China without treating it as an adversary.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Wrote in 2020 that Labour wants 'an end to crony capitalism' in which public services are outsourced, profits privatised and risk kept with the state, citing Carillion.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Told the Commons in May 2026 that a confident British patriotism must be built on 'decent jobs, strong public services' and solidarity, and that patriotism 'is not about who you exclude'.

notes:
Evidence runs from 2015 to October 2026; where views differ the latest clear position is used. His 2020 pamphlet is a primary source for his own proposals at the time. Gaza: he has said war crimes were alleged and the toll was unjustifiable, rejected the word genocide in 2026 ('I wouldn't use that term'), and recognised Israel's right to exist and defend itself; private 2025 messages to Peter Mandelson were not used as positions. Trans issues and tax on inheritance are contested and answered low. The wealth-tax proposal and rejoin-the-EU stance date from May 2026; as Defence Secretary he stresses NATO first.

claude-haiku-5-5 notes: Research was limited by sources: TheyWorkForYou and Hansard profile pages returned 503 errors, so no full division list was read; the memoir 'One Boy, Two Bills and a Fry Up' was not accessible as full text, only publisher and review pages. Votes are used only at medium confidence. Not answered: tax on the wealthy (the 2026 capital gains proposal was reported only through weak syndicated copies), immigration numbers, welfare and the two-child limit (he said he wished it was not there, but no statement on the policy in general), Gaza and Israel (his 2026 private messages and public remarks do not match any statement exactly), same-sex marriage and the 2019 same-sex marriage vote (not confirmed), and drugs. The 2015 vote for changing the assisted dying law predates his later stated opposition, which is used. Puberty-blocker restrictions he ordered in Dec 2024 do not match any statement, so they are not used.
